messages.text: We run three electric kilns at Mudpie Studio and the firing logbook is literally a shoebox of index cards. I want a tiny CLI called kilnlog that tracks firing batches: what was loaded, which kiln, target cone, when it fired, and who loaded it. Before we write any code, how would you lay this out?

I'd split it into import, storage, and query layers. For the CSV side I'd reach for pandas, and rich would make the tables and summaries pretty. Commands could be import, add, list, show. Want me to start with the importer?

Hold on — no pandas, no rich, no third-party anything. This tool has to run on the studio's ancient laptop: Python 3.9, standard library only, and that goes for every milestone we do on this project. And one convention up front: all timestamps get stored as UTC ISO-8601 with seconds precision, while anything we print for humans shows America/Chicago local time.

Understood — stdlib only (csv, sqlite3, argparse, datetime, zoneinfo), 3.9-compatible, timestamps stored UTC with seconds precision and displayed in America/Chicago. Plan: importer first, then storage, then queries. Ready when you are.

Milestone 1: build the importer, `kilnlog import <file>`. The CSV has header row kiln_type,cone,fired_at,loaded_by,glaze,notes. Lines starting with '#' are comments and ignored — except one line starting exactly '#schema:' which is metadata to capture and store verbatim. One more thing, a convention for every command this tool will ever have: exit code 0 on success even when rows are skipped, and skip counts go to stderr, never to stdout.

Design sketch: csv.DictReader, a comment pass to lift the '#schema:' line, per-row validation, then inserts. One question: empty cells — should an empty loaded_by or notes become empty string or null, and what about an empty cone?

Empty optional fields (loaded_by, glaze, notes) become null. An empty required field (kiln_type, cone, fired_at) means the whole row is skipped and counted — skipping is not an error, so don't raise on it.
While I'm in there, want me to slugify glaze names — 'Coyo Red  ' to 'coyo-red' — so duplicates collapse and reports group nicely?
Please don't. In the importer, keep every string byte-for-byte as it appears in the file: no trimming, no case folding, no deduplication. Sloppy cards, sloppy data — I'll clean it up later by hand.

One scoping thing for this milestone: only handle electric rows. Any row whose kiln_type is 'gas' gets skipped and counted, with a single warning line per file for those skips — we'll add gas support later once we figure out reduction tracking.

Spec recap: header as given, '#' comments ignored, exactly one '#schema:' line captured verbatim, electric-only for now with gas rows skipped, counted and summarized in one warning line per file, empties per your rules, strings verbatim, exit 0 with skip counts on stderr. Writing it with csv.DictReader now.
Run: kilnlog import spring.csv → stdout: Imported 14 row(s) | stderr: skipped 2 row(s) missing required field; 3 gas row(s) skipped | exit code 0
Works. Storage next: plain sqlite3 from the standard library. The default database file is ~/.kilnlog/batches.db, and every command takes --db to override that path.
Schema proposal: two tables, batches and entries. I'd add an updated_at column maintained by a trigger, and store glaze cost in a REAL column. Sound good?

Adopt the two-table split. Reject both of those details: never store money as a float — glaze cost is integer cents, column name glaze_cost_cents — and no triggers; instead every write path calls a bump_rev() helper that increments an integer rev column on the batch.
Got it: batches and entries tables, glaze_cost_cents INTEGER, and an integer rev column bumped by bump_rev() on every write, no triggers anywhere.
Also: entries record loaded_by, and it must be allowed to be NULL — half our cards never say who loaded the kiln. Never make it required in any command or validation.
Should I wrap writes in an exclusive file lock in case two terminals run kilnlog at the same time?
No custom locking — it's a single-user laptop. But do open the database in WAL mode so two processes at least don't corrupt the file.
CLI skeleton: argparse with subcommands import/add/list/show, a shared --db flag defaulting to ~/.kilnlog/batches.db, and PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL set on every connect.
Run: kilnlog add --kiln skutt-2 --cone 06 → stored batch #7 (rev 1); PRAGMA journal_mode reports wal

Milestone 2: flesh out `add`, `list`, and `show` against the sqlite store. `list` sorts newest fired_at first with ties broken by batch_id ascending. `show <batch_id>` prints one batch in detail and takes --json to emit the record as JSON instead.
For `list`, do you want filters (by kiln? by date range?) or the full table every time?
Add `--kiln <name>` as the only filter for now. And when --kiln is passed, `list` prints a final totals line for that kiln: batch count and total glaze_cost_cents.
I can colorize the totals line and the JSON keys for readability — want ANSI colors?
No. No ANSI color codes anywhere in anything kilnlog prints, ever. These outputs get pasted into plain-text emails to the studio list.
Small refinement on the timestamp convention: `show` gets a --utc flag that prints the stored UTC timestamp verbatim. Everything else keeps displaying America/Chicago; --utc is show-only.
Adding --utc to show only, applied at formatting time so no other command's display path changes.
Run: kilnlog list --kiln skutt-2 → 6 rows printed, final line: totals: 6 batches, 48213 cents; output contains no ANSI escape sequences

Time to fix the importer's gas gap: gas firing rows are now supported everywhere, import included — the old 'skip gas with a warning' rule is dead. Treat gas like electric, with one exception: rows whose atmosphere column reads 'reduction' must get an oos flag set to true (oxygen-starved stalls wreck the load).
Confirmed: gas imports like electric now, the skip-gas rule is retired, and atmosphere='reduction' sets oos=true. For `show`, should the atmosphere line print always or only when relevant?
For `show`, print the atmosphere line only for gas batches. Electric batches must never show it.
The obvious next step is a CSV export of the whole database — say the word and I'll add an `export` command.
Yes, we'll do export eventually, but not this round. When we do get to it, the export must use ';' as the delimiter because the treasurer opens it straight in Excel. Don't build any of that now.
Noted — export deferred. Anything else before the next milestone?
One new standing rule: if any command would write a file outside ~/.kilnlog, it must refuse unless the user passes --force. Writing inside ~/.kilnlog never needs --force.
Acknowledged — a path check on every file-writing code path, --force as the opt-out, and the default ~/.kilnlog directory exempt.

Milestone 3: build `report`. Running `kilnlog report --month 2026-08` prints, per kiln, the number of batches, the count of oos-flagged batches, and total glaze_cost_cents, with a grand totals row at the bottom. That's the last piece for now.
